text:
A: Hiya! Hello! Can you hear me alright?
B: Hi! Yes, hello, I can hear you. I'm Charlotte, I'm in Woking.
A: I'm Donna, Thornton Heath. I loved your hair in your photo, by the way, and your room, it looks like something out of a magazine, honestly.
B: Oh, thank you, that's so nice! It's only the spare room, it's mostly where I do my emails. Erm, I saw your tabard, are you in healthcare?
A: Yeah, senior care assistant, residential home in Norbury. Twelve-hour shifts. I'm on my feet all day, I'm always shattered on my day off.
B: I thought you might be. I'm sort of healthcare-adjacent, I'm in operations for dental practices. Nine clinics. So I'm on the other end, I'm the one doing the rotas, sorry!
A: Oh, so you're the one! No, I'm joking. But you know what gets me, at our place, the agency staff get the good shifts and the ones that's been there years get the rubbish ones. I've been there longer than the manager, near enough, and I'm still not team leader. The families ask for me by name and everything.
B: That's really unfair, to be honest. I'd want to keep someone like that happy, the families asking for you is gold. Have you said anything?
A: I've said it! Loads of times. They just go, mm, we'll see.
B: Do you know what I mean, though, sometimes you have to put it in writing. Like, here's what I do, here's the feedback. They can't ignore it then.
A: That's true, actually. I never thought of writing it down. You sound like you'd be a good manager.
B: Ha, I try. My practice managers might say otherwise.
A: Have you got kids? I always ask, sorry, I'm nosy.
B: Erm, no, not yet. Just the dog. Have you, I mean, the baby in your photo, is that yours?
A: My granddaughter! I'm a nan. Shanice's little one. Honestly she's the best thing, I go round Mitcham every chance I get.
B: Aw, that's lovely. She looks gorgeous. Erm, what do you like doing, when you're not working?
A: Soaps, Love Island, TikTok. Bit of shopping. I got a lovely bag in TK Maxx last week, half price. And I love a show, but only for my birthday, the West End's so dear.
B: Oh, I love musicals! We saw Les Mis in the summer, I cried all the way through.
A: Me too, I cry at anything! I cry at adverts. Clive won't sit next to me at the cinema.
B: Tom's the same! He just passes me tissues without looking. Do you go away much?
A: Jamaica, to see family. But I hate flying, I need a drink and my headphones and I'm still gripping the seat.
B: Oh my God, me too. I'm a terrible flyer. I need a glass of wine and Tom holding my hand on take-off, it's so embarrassing.
A: It's not embarrassing! Last time, this man next to me, he said, you was shaking the whole row. I said, sorry, I'm praying. Is that, erm, are we allowed to talk about anything?
B: I think so, I keep asking that as well. I'm never sure if I'm doing it right.
